liebermann.date: early 11th century; p. 364 another hand, 11th century; p. 418 f. late 11th century
liebermann.notes: An early 11th-century manuscript, mainly homiletic and canonistic, given by Leofric to Exeter Cathedral as 'Scriftboc on Englisc'; related to C, G, P. In other hands it adds Excommunicatio III (p. 364), the Confessionale and Poenitentiale Pseudo-Egberti, and at the end (late 11th century) Mirce, Að and Had, these taken from doi. It was copied in Harley 438.

wormald.liebermann_date: early 11th century; p. 364 another hand, 11th century; p. 418 f. late 11th century
wormald.wormald_date: s. xi¹–xi^med (Table 4.1, p. 164). Part I (section a), pp. i–xii, 1–294) s. xi¹ (p. 220); Part II section b) s. xi^med (p. 222); section c) confession forms in an Exeter-type hand; additions on pp. 360–1 s. xiᵉˣ and Excom III (p. 364) s. xiiⁱⁿ (Table 4.5, p. 222); legal tracts (pp. 418–20) undated (p. 223)
wormald.wormald_origin: Worcester/Exeter (Table 4.1, p. 164). Section a) 'almost certainly' in a Worcester hand (p. 220); section b) of unknown origin but its content points to Wulfstan's Worcester (p. 222). At Exeter by the early fourteenth century; probably the 'Canon in Latin and Confessional in English' (Scriftboc) of Bishop Leofric's (1046–72) list; Exeter scribes (incl. perhaps Leofric himself) added to both parts; presumably given by the Dean and Chapter to Parker (pp. 220, 223 and nn. 225–7). The two halves may not have been united before the Exeter additions; Bishop Lyfing (Crediton 1027–46, Worcester 1038–40, 1041–6) is another candidate unifier (pp. 220, 223).
wormald.laws: Section c) (pp. 418–20): Mirce, Að (Að 1, Að 2; the priest clause linked to a tariff for the seven holy orders), Had — the status tracts given in full in CCCC 201, but without Norðleod, which may point to Worcester interests (Table 4.5, p. 222; p. 223; cf. p. 248 n. 332). Section d) addition: Excom III (p. 364, s. xiiⁱⁿ), the formula Liebermann printed from this MS (p. 211 n. 196; Table 4.5).
wormald.other_contents: Part I, section a): a Worcester form of the Wulfstan 'Canon Collection' (Table 4.4): complete Pseudo-Theodore penitential (Thorpe's sole edition), canonical texts pp. 94–110 (Atto of Vercelli etc.), Excerptiones (Nero/Thorpe version) from p. 111 after lost quire(s) (chapter-list survives), consanguinity diagram pp. 132–3, Aachen 816/Hrabanus on clerical ranks, Amalarius/Regularis Concordia sequence, Abbo's sermon (pp. 253–8) followed by a blessing of oils, liturgy, Adso on Antichrist, Liber Scintillarum. Part II (Table 4.5): b) Ælfric's OE Pastoral Letters for Wulfstan (II, III), the OE 'Confessional' and 'Penitential' of Pseudo-Ecgberht; c) forms of confession and absolution (p. 365) and the legal tracts; d) Exeter additions under Leofric: Ælfric's first Pastoral Letter (for Wulfsige), Ælfric homily on the apostles' mission, Inst. Pol. XXIV on clerical ranks, OE versions of Abbo's penitential sermons, canons on excommunication, a verse 'Invectivum in damnantes coniugia sacerdotum' (s. xiᵉˣ), Excom III.
wormald.overview: Corpus 190 is really two books. The first is a Worcester copy, of the first half of the eleventh century, of the Latin church-law collection associated with Archbishop Wulfstan, in a form that Wormald regards as a bundle of raw ingredients rather than a finished arrangement; the second, of the mid-eleventh century, gathers Ælfric's Old English pastoral letters and two penitentials and was enlarged at Exeter under Bishop Leofric, whose list of gifts to his cathedral very probably describes the combined volume. Its only Anglo-Saxon legal texts are the short status tracts Mirce, Að and Had, added at an uncertain date to the vernacular half, together with a twelfth-century excommunication formula (Liebermann's Excom III). Wormald reads the tracts as part of a continuing effort to render church-law material in English.
wormald.liebermann_superseded: Liebermann treated it as a single early-eleventh-century book with later additions (Excom III '11th century', Mirce–Að–Had 'late 11th century'); Wormald shows it is two distinct halves — a s. xi¹ Worcester Latin canon collection and a s. xi^med vernacular penitential collection — not demonstrably united before the Exeter additions, dates Excom III s. xiiⁱⁿ, and leaves the date of the legal tracts open (pp. 220–3; Table 4.5, p. 222).
wormald.key_quote: Latin 'Canon' was counterpointed by Old English 'Scriftboc'. (p. 223)
wormald.doubts: GUIDE: Liebermann says Mirce, Að, Had were added 'late 11th century' and 'taken from doi'; Wormald says where and when they were added is unclear (p. 223), and links them to the collection preserved complete in CCCC 201. Sigla: 'W' for the Homily editors, 'X' for Aronstam; Ker no. 45. Harley 438 copy (guide) not mentioned by Wormald here. Corpus 190 is really two books. The first is a Worcester copy, of the first half of the eleventh century, of the Latin church-law collection associated with Archbishop Wulfstan, in a form that Wormald regards as a bundle of raw ingredients rather than a finished arrangement; the second, of the mid-eleventh century, gathers Ælfric's Old English pastoral letters and two penitentials and was enlarged at Exeter under Bishop Leofric, whose list of gifts to his cathedral very probably describes the combined volume.
